rawFindings.title: Reports already-quantified spaces and produces invalid fixes
rawFindings.explanation: The new matcher flags any run of two spaces even when it is immediately followed by a regex quantifier. For a pattern such as `/  +/`, the two literal spaces are intentionally quantified by `+`; the rule now reports them and the fixer replaces only the spaces, leaving the existing quantifier after the replacement.
rawFindings.suggestion: Restore the quantifier-aware check so runs immediately followed by `+`, `*`, `{`, or `?` are not matched, or include the following quantifier in the replacement logic.
rawFindings.failureAfterChange: Input `var foo = /  +/;` now reports an error and `--fix` produces `var foo = / {2}+/;`, which is not a valid JavaScript regular expression literal.
